# truenas_s3_config (Resource)

Manages the TrueNAS S3 service configuration (s3.config / s3.update; TrueNAS 27.0 and later). This is a singleton resource: there is exactly one S3 configuration per TrueNAS system, so it is never created or deleted on TrueNAS; Terraform create/update call s3.update, and Terraform delete only removes the resource from state. Buckets have no TrueNAS API: they are created through the S3 protocol (CreateBucket) by an access key with manage_buckets, under managed_root_dataset. Turn the service on with truenas_service ("s3"). See the "S3 state backend" guide.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The S3 service configuration (TrueNAS 27.0 and later). One per system:
# this resource is never created or deleted on TrueNAS, only updated.
resource "truenas_dataset" "s3" {
  name = "tank/s3"
}

resource "truenas_s3_config" "s3" {
  listeners = [
    { address = "0.0.0.0", port = 9000 }, # plaintext on every address
  ]
  region    = "us-east-1"
  log_level = "NOTICE"

  # Buckets created through the S3 protocol (CreateBucket, by a key with
  # manage_buckets = true) get a dataset under this one. There is no
  # TrueNAS API for buckets.
  managed_root_dataset = truenas_dataset.s3.name

  default_audit = ["PutObject", "DeleteObject", "CreateBucket", "DeleteBucket"]
}

# Turn the service on.
resource "truenas_service" "s3" {
  service = "s3"
  enable  = true
  running = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `certificate` (Number) ID of the certificate the TLS listeners serve (truenas_certificate.x.id). Unset (null) serves them with the UI certificate; removing it from the configuration clears a certificate set before.
- `default_audit` (List of String) S3 actions audited on every bucket that does not set its own audit list, e.g. ["PutObject", "DeleteObject"]. ["ALL"] audits everything (the API's "ALL"); an empty list audits nothing.
- `default_audit_overflow` (String) What an audited request gets when no audit record slot is free: DROP sheds the record, BACKPRESSURE delays the request.
- `global_grants` (Attributes List) Grants that apply to every bucket; the list replaces the current one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--global_grants))
- `listeners` (Attributes List) Where the S3 service listens, at most eight entries. An empty list listens on every address on port 9000 in plaintext. Changing it restarts the service. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--listeners))
- `log_level` (String) Least serious log record the S3 service keeps: ERROR, WARNING, NOTICE, INFO (one record per request) or DEBUG.
- `managed_root_dataset` (String) Dataset under which buckets created through the S3 protocol get their datasets, e.g. tank/s3. Null (or empty) means buckets cannot be created through S3.
- `region` (String) Region name echoed to clients, us-east-1 shaped (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; at most 63). Empty accepts whatever a client sends.
- `servers` (Number) Reactor threads serving the listen addresses (1-12).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Fixed identifier for this singleton resource: always "s3_config".

<a id="nestedatt--global_grants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `global_grants`

Required:

- `access` (String) READONLY, WRITEONLY, READWRITE, or DENY (refuses every operation, outranks the bucket owner).
- `principal_type` (String) USER, GROUP or EVERYONE (everyone with a valid access key).

Optional:

- `xid` (Number) uid of the user or gid of the group. Required for USER and GROUP, forbidden for EVERYONE.


<a id="nestedatt--listeners"></a>
### Nested Schema for `listeners`

Required:

- `address` (String) IP address to listen on (s3.bindip_choices): a static address, a loopback or a wildcard (0.0.0.0, ::).

Optional:

- `port` (Number) TCP port to listen on. Default 9000.
- `tls` (Boolean) Serve this address over TLS with `certificate` (which must then be set). Default false.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Singleton: any id is accepted and normalised to "s3_config".
terraform import truenas_s3_config.s3 s3_config
```
